signals.title: [Quantization] Support per-block FP8 for Quark fused MoE layers
signals.text: ## Purpose `QuarkConfig._is_fp8_w8a8` already accepts per-block (128x128) FP8 weights, and #47972 added `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` so that **linear** layers can consume them. `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` was never updated, so it still rejects the `per_block` qscheme: ``` ValueError: For FP8 Fused MoE layers, only per-tensor and per-channel scales for weights and activations are supported. Found per_block, per_group ``` The result is an asymmetry: for a Quark checkpoint whose routed experts are quantized per-block, every linear layer loads fine but the MoE layers cannot be built at all. ### Concrete case: the MTP layer of an MoE model Models that ship an MTP (multi-token prediction) draft layer make this asymmetry easy to see, because vLLM builds the MTP layer from the *same* decoder-layer class as the main model. For `Qwen3.5-397B-A17B`, `Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor` instantiates `Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(layer_type="full_attention")`, which for an MoE config contains a complete `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` with all 512 routed experts. Broken down by quantization path (`{i}` runs over `mtp_num_hidden_layers`, default 1): | Module | vLLM layer | Quant path | Status | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `mtp.embed_tokens` | `VocabParallelEmbedding` | — | not quantized | | `mtp.fc` | `ColumnParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.norm`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_hidden`, `mtp.pre_fc_norm_embedding` | `Qwen3_5RMSNorm` | — | not quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.self_attn.qkv_proj` | `QKVParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.self_attn.o_proj` | `RowParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.gate` | `ReplicatedLinear`, built with `quant_config=None` | — | never quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert_gate` | `ReplicatedLinear`, built with `quant_config=None` | — | never quantized | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert.gate_up_proj` | `MergedColumnParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.shared_expert.down_proj` | `RowParallelLinear` | linear | supported (#47972) | | **`mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.experts`** | **`RoutedExperts`** | **fused MoE** | **rejected — fixed by this PR** | `mtp.layers.{i}.mlp.experts` is the only module in the MTP stack that takes the fused-MoE path, and it is the only one that fails. It is also not a small module: with `hidden_size=4096`, `moe_intermediate_size=1024` and 512 experts it holds roughly 6.4B parameters, so leaving it unquantized is not a practical workaround. Two related details worth noting: - `mlp.gate` and `mlp.shared_expert_gate` are constructed with a hardcoded `quant_config=None`, so they are never quantized regardless of the Quark config. - When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` is enabled and the shared expert is not excluded from quantization, `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` sets `shared_expert = None` and folds the shared expert into the routed-expert tensors, which moves those weights onto the fused-MoE path as well. ## Changes All changes are inside the existing `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod`, following the `BLOCK` strategy of `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` rather than adding a new class: the weight, bias, input-scale and kernel-setup code is shared with the per-tensor and per-channel paths, and only the scale layout, the scale parameter name and a few flags differ. - `__init__`: accept `per_block`; read `block_size` from the weight config; use `kFp8Static128BlockSym` / `kFp8Dynamic128Sym` for backend selection; require dynamic activation quantization for per-block weights; select the scale parameter name (`weight_scale_inv` for per-block, `weight_scale` otherwise) the way `Fp8MoEMethod` already does. - `create_weights`: propagate `layer.weight_block_size`; validate that `intermediate_size_per_partition` is divisible by `block_n` (and by `block_k` when TP > 1) so misalignment fails at weight-creation time rather than silently producing wrong results in the kernel; allocate block-grid weight scales, register them as `w13_weight_scale_inv` / `w2_weight_scale_inv`, and tag them with `FusedMoeWeightScaleSupported.BLOCK` so `RoutedExperts.weight_loader` shards them on the block grid instead of per row. - `process_weights_after_loading`, `_setup_kernel` and `get_fused_moe_quant_config`: look the weight scales up through the selected name, and pass `block_shape` through to `make_fp8_moe_quant_config`. The per-tensor requantization loop and the per-channel `unsqueeze` in `process_weights_after_loading` remain guarded on `weight_qscheme`, and per-block weights require dynamic activations so the static input-scale branch is skipped. The only per-block change there is routing the fnuz normalization through the selected scale name, so per-block also works on MI300. The per-tensor and per-channel paths are unchanged: `block_shape` stays `None`, the scale parameters keep the `weight_scale` name, and the scale shapes are identical to before. ### Why the per-block scales are named `weight_scale_inv` Block-quantized checkpoints store their per-block scales as `weight_scale_inv` (the deepseek-v3 convention Quark follows), and `RoutedExperts.load_weights` derives the parameter name from the checkpoint tensor name by replacing only the module-path portion and carrying the suffix over verbatim — `...experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv` resolves to `w2_weight_scale_inv`, with no aliasing step in between. Registering the scales under `w2_weight_scale` therefore made every per-block checkpoint fail to load: ``` AttributeError: Layer mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts has no parameter 'w2_weight_scale_inv' for checkpoint weight 'mtp.layers.0.mlp.experts.0.down_proj.weight_scale_inv' ``` Both names hold the same quantity (a dequantization multiplier, multiplied into the block-scaled GEMM), so this is purely a lookup-key mismatch and it always fails loudly. ## Test Plan Added to `tests/quantization/test_quark.py`: - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_requires_block_size` — a per-block weight config without `block_size` is rejected. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_rejects_per_block_static_input` — static activations are rejected for per-block weights. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_weight_shapes` — `w13`/`w2` weight and scale shapes, that the scales are registered under the `weight_scale_inv` name and not under `weight_scale`, and that both scales carry the `BLOCK` loader attribute. - `test_quark_w8a8_fp8_moe_per_block_rejects_misaligned_partition` — a partition size that is not a multiple of `block_n` fails during `create_weights`. ```bash pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block ``` ## Test Result Hardware: 1x MI355X (gfx950), ROCm. Checkpoint: `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` re-quantized with AMD Quark from `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8` into an NVFP4 backbone plus a per-block FP8 MTP layer (775 MTP modules per-block FP8, 10 kept in BF16 through `exclude`). This reproduces the asymmetry described above: the MTP `mlp.experts` module is per-block FP8 while the main model is NVFP4. ### Load and module routing TP=1, `speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}`: | Model | Module | Bound method | | --- | --- | --- | | target | 40 MoE layers | `QuarkNvfp4MoEMethod` | | drafter (MTP) | `mlp.experts.routed_experts` | `QuarkW8A8Fp8MoEMethod` | | drafter (MTP) | `self_attn.qkv_proj`, `self_attn.o_proj`, `shared_expert.{gate_up,down}_proj` | `QuarkLinearMethod` / `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock` | | drafter (MTP) | `fc`, `mlp.gate`, `mlp.shared_expert_gate` | `UnquantizedLinearMethod` | Backends selected, with no fallbacks reported: ``` Selected TritonFp8BlockScaledMMKernel for QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock Using TRITON Fp8 MoE backend Using 'EMULATION' NvFp4 MoE backend ``` ### MTP acceptance `Draft acceptance rate: 94.7%-95.9%`, acceptance length 1.96 out of a maximum of 2 for `num_speculative_tokens=1`. This is the most direct evidence that the per-block expert weights and scales are loaded correctly: a scale mismatch drives acceptance towards 0. ### GSM8K `lm_eval` 5-shot over the full 1319 questions, chat template with thinking disabled: | Filter | exact_match | | --- | --- | | flexible-extract | 0.9629 ± 0.0052 | | strict-match | 0.9636 ± 0.0052 | ### Unit tests ``` pytest tests/quantization/test_quark.py -k per_block 8 passed, 35 deselected ``` This covers the four new MoE tests above together with the pre-existing per-block linear tests from #47972, which still pass.

signals.title: [CI][AMD] Improve Kubernetes failure diagnostics
signals.text: AMD CI failures currently flood the Buildkite log with host-oriented diagnostics and can leave native or single-node Docker work behind after timeouts and signals. This change keeps the terminal summary short, uploads pod-aware diagnostics as a Buildkite artifact, and selectively incorporates the durable teardown logic. The diagnostics and teardown now share one failure path so cleanup cannot suppress the artifact or alter the original test status. - Capture cgroup v1/v2 CPU, memory, OOM, pressure, PID, I/O, process, mount, `/dev/shm`, GPU, and network evidence in `artifacts/amd-ci-failure-diagnostics/.../diagnostics.log`. - Keep failure output to a three-line summary, preserve the original exit status, and retain non-GPU diagnostics for CPU-only jobs. - Track native and single-node Docker tests in dedicated process groups, enforce the remaining CI timeout, terminate escaped tagged descendants, and clean only job-labeled containers with bounded Docker commands.

signals.title: [ROCm] Give EngineCore cleanup grace after request abort
signals.text: AMD CI exposed a shutdown race where `shutdown_timeout=0` aborted requests as intended but also gave EngineCore no time to release ROCm resources before SIGKILL. This change preserves immediate request abort while giving the ROCm EngineCore process manager a bounded 60-second cleanup grace when both the configured and remaining process timeouts are zero. It keeps exhausted budgets for positive shutdown timeouts unchanged and extends the DP supervisor's outer deadline to cover the cleanup window. - The motivating failure is [AMD CI build 12007](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/12007/list?sid=019ffc53-a1ab-472f-8b77-7c52a7d6edc0&tab=output). - The final request completed successfully, but EngineCore was force-killed immediately and GPU memory remained at 11.72 GB for the full 120-second release wait. - The `LLM()` to `vllm_runner()` migration does not cover this path because these tests launch a real out-of-process `vllm serve` server. - Add a ROCm-only 60-second EngineCore process cleanup grace when both the configured request timeout and remaining process timeout are zero. - Keep `shutdown_timeout=0` inside EngineCore so in-flight requests are still aborted immediately. - Preserve exhausted positive shutdown deadlines instead of accidentally granting them a fresh cleanup window. - Extend the DP supervisor's outer wait budget so it does not kill the process tree before EngineCore cleanup can finish. - Add manager and DP supervisor regression coverage in the existing test files.

signals.title: [CI] Harden RemoteVLLMServer GPU cleanup checks
signals.text: This PR is stacked on `akaratza_enginecore_shutdown` and hardens `RemoteVLLMServer` cleanup after a server exits. GPU baselines and cleanup waits are tracked per child-visible physical device, including overlapping multi-server scopes, so one leaked allocation cannot be hidden by a later aggregate baseline. Unavailable telemetry and timed-out cleanup now fail closed and retain affected-scope state until recovery can be verified. The test server's outer termination window also covers the EngineCore cleanup grace introduced by the first PR. - Prevent a teardown failure from ratcheting leaked VRAM into the next server's `_pre_server_gpu_memory` baseline. - Measure the physical devices selected by each child server's visibility environment on ROCm and CUDA. - Preserve parent-logical ordinal measurement on XPU, where `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` cannot consume physical or tile mask IDs. - Retain cleanup poison while intentionally concurrent servers make recovery unverifiable, and fail closed for unsafe partial coverage. - Merge partially overlapping scopes and use the earliest per-device baseline so a broader server cannot hide a leak behind an earlier sibling's allocation. - Keep GPU-less render-server tests outside GPU release accounting.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Fall back when zentorch import fails
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52238. On AMD Zen CPU builds, a non-`ImportError` raised while importing zentorch currently escapes `cpu_platform_plugin`. Platform discovery then silently drops the CPU plugin and selects `UnspecifiedPlatform`. This change logs the underlying zentorch import failure and falls back to the standard `CpuPlatform`. A CPU-only regression test covers an incompatible shared library represented by `OSError`. I reviewed the issue comments and searched open PRs for both `#52238` and the zentorch CPU-platform import path. No overlapping open PR was found. AI assistance was used to develop and test this change. I reviewed every changed line of code and the regression test, and I understand and can defend the change end-to-end. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py -q .venv/bin/ruff check --ignore ISC004 vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py .venv/bin/ruff format --check vllm/platforms/__init__.py tests/test_zen_cpu_platform_detection.py ``` The repository pre-commit hooks also ran during commit. ## Test Result - Before the implementation, the new regression test failed with the simulated `OSError: incompatible shared library` escaping platform detection. - After the implementation: `5 passed in 0.62s`. - Ruff check and format check passed. - All commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy and repository policy checks. - An additional platform-plugin test was attempted with its required dummy plugin installed. Its platform assertion passed, but the process later segfaulted in the existing macOS PyTorch global cleanup path at `torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache`; this is outside the changed code. - Model evaluations were not run because this change does not affect model outputs, accuracy, or serving behavior. No documentation update is needed.
signals.author: luyixiao95

signals.title: [Model][Generative Recommendation] Add HSTU model support to vLLM
signals.text: ## Purpose This PR adds HSTU-based generative recommendation model support to vLLM. HSTU is a ranking model architecture designed for generative recommendation. Unlike traditional language models, HSTU does not autoregressively generate text tokens. Instead, it synchronously computes ranking scores for all candidate items in a request. The goal of this change is to enable generative recommendation models to reuse the existing vLLM and large-model serving ecosystem, including: - Hugging Face model and configuration loading. - vLLM model registration. - GPU model execution. - Attention backend selection. - Optimized CUDA operators. - Request batching and scheduling. - Asynchronous output handling. - CUDA Graph execution. - Future distributed inference and online serving infrastructure. Generative recommendation and large language models have several common characteristics. Both can be represented as sequence models, use embedding layers and transformer-style computation, and benefit from optimized attention kernels, GPU batching, asynchronous execution, and production-level model serving infrastructure. By integrating HSTU into vLLM, generative recommendation models can reuse the existing large-model ecosystem instead of maintaining an independent inference stack. ## Inference Paradigm Although HSTU and large language models share several model and runtime components, their inference semantics are different. | Aspect | Large language model | Generative recommendation model | | --- | --- | --- | | Decode behavior | Autoregressively generates one token at a time | Synchronously computes scores for all candidates in a request | | Model output | Vocabulary logits for the next token | One ranking score for each candidate item | | Sampling | Requires token sampling and token ID generation | Does not generate a sampled token | | Request progress | Continues until the requested number of tokens is generated | Completes after all candidate scores are returned | | Output format | Usually `[num_tokens, vocab_size]` | Packed candidate-score output | | Scheduler signal | Uses sampled token IDs to update request state | Uses candidate scores to complete the request | The default vLLM generation path is designed around language-model execution: 1. Run the model forward pass. 2. Produce vocabulary logits. 3. Invoke the token sampler. 4. Generate token IDs. 5. Update the request state. 6. Continue decoding until the request is finished. This flow cannot be directly reused for HSTU because HSTU produces candidate ranking scores rather than vocabulary logits. Passing HSTU outputs through the normal sampler would incorrectly interpret candidate scores as vocabulary logits and could produce invalid token IDs. Therefore, this PR adds a score-only execution path: 1. Run the HSTU forward pass. 2. Extract the score corresponding to each candidate item. 3. Convert candidate IDs and scores into `LogprobsTensors`. 4. Return the scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. 5. Skip the standard token sampler. 6. Skip generated-token state updates. 7. Complete the request after all candidate scores are returned. The scheduler is also updated to support score-only recommendation requests. A request can be completed after candidate scores are produced even when no `new_token_ids` are returned. ## Implementation Overview This PR contains five main categories of changes. ### 1. Model Structure and Model Registration Files: - `vllm/model_executor/models/hstu.py` - `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` - `tests/models/registry.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU model implementation. - Add HSTU embedding layers, transformer blocks, normalization layers, and prediction heads. - Register the HSTU model with vLLM. - Support Hugging Face HSTU model loading. - Add HSTU to the model registry test data. - Add model registration and model import coverage. ### 2. Model Configuration and Configuration Registration Files: - `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/__init__.py` - `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/hstu.py` Changes: - Add HSTU-specific configuration classes. - Support HSTU model and task configuration fields. - Support `model_type = "hstu"`. - Convert HSTU configuration data from Hugging Face configuration files into the vLLM configuration representation. - Preserve compatibility with the existing vLLM configuration loading flow. ### 3. Model Operators and Operator Registration Files: - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/hstu_attn.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/backends/registry.py` - `vllm/v1/attention/selector.py` Changes: - Add the HSTU attention backend. - Integrate the external HSTU variable-length attention operator. - Register the HSTU attention backend with vLLM. - Automatically select `HSTU_ATTN` for HSTU or generative recommendation models when no explicit backend is configured. - Preserve explicit attention backend configuration as the highest-priority option. - Validate unsupported attention combinations and return clear errors. - Pass per-request context and candidate metadata to the HSTU attention implementation. Automatic backend selection is only applied when the user has not explicitly selected an attention backend. This preserves the existing backend override behavior. ### 4. Model Runner V1 Adaptation File: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` Changes: - Add generative recommendation metadata collection. - Add HSTU candidate score extraction. - Pass HSTU metadata through the forward context. - Bypass the standard token sampler for HSTU requests. - Return candidate scores through the prompt-logprobs output path. - Add recommendation-specific request completion handling. - Preserve the existing execution path for non-HSTU models. ### 5. Model Runner V2 Adaptation Files: - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/gr_state.py` - `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/async_utils.py` - `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py` Changes: - Add `GRState` for request-scoped generative recommendation state. - Store user IDs, candidate count, prompt token IDs, and request stage. - Move candidate score extraction from the Model Runner into `GRState`. - Convert packed HSTU outputs into `LogprobsTensors`. - Add asynchronous score output handling. - Return candidate scores through `prompt_logprobs_dict`. - Skip token sampling and token-state updates for HSTU requests. - Complete score-only requests in the scheduler when candidate scores are available. - Preserve the one-token early-return behavior required by generative recommendation inputs. ## Test Plan ### 1. Environment Setup The operator is installed inside the following NVIDIA PyTorch container:`nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:26.06-py3` Install the required system dependency:`apt update && apt install -y libxcb1` ### 2.HSTU Operator Installation and Validation The HSTU attention operator is provided by the NVIDIA `recsys-examples` repository. Clone the recsys-examples repository:`git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/recsys-examples.git && cd recsys-examples/corelib/hstu` For H20 and other Hopper-based devices, enter the corresponding device directory before compiling: `cd hopper` Install the HSTU operator:`Install the HSTU operator:` After the compilation completes successfully, validate the operator installation with: `python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu_op.py` ### 3.vLLM Installation Clone the vLLM repository:`git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git && cd vllm` Install the current vLLM source with CUDA support:`VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda pip install -v -e .` ### 4. HSTU Model Inference: After the HSTU changes are included in vLLM, run:`python vllm/tests/models/generativemodel/test_hstu.py` This test validates: * HSTU model loading. * HSTU configuration loading. * HSTU model registration. * HSTU attention backend initialization. * HSTU forward execution. * Candidate score extraction. * Candidate ID and score formatting. * Score-only execution without token sampling. * Recommendation request completion. * Model Runner integration. * CUDA Graph execution. ### 5. Model Registry and Hugging Face Loading Run the model registry tests:`pytest -q tests/models/test_registry.py -k HSTUForCausalLM` This validates that: * HSTUForCausalLM is registered. * The HSTU model class can be imported. * Hugging Face model metadata is available. * The HSTU configuration can be loaded. * The vLLM model registry can resolve the HSTU model. ## Test Result ### HSTU Operator The test returned like: ```text Input q shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Output shape: torch.Size([40, 4096]) Run success ``` ### HSTU Model Inference The test returned candidate IDs and their corresponding ranking scores. A truncated example of the output is: ```text Request 0: 12676:0.6602 47052:0.5078 45082:0.4336 79131:0.3984 34671:0.4844 5695:0.4570 95647:0.1777 60217:0.5273 70284:0.4258 16361:0.4238 Request 1: 8023:0.4863 24460:0.6094 ... ``` Each line follows the format:`Each line follows the format:` The output confirms that HSTU synchronously computes the scores of all candidates for a request and returns the scores through the generative recommendation output path. The test also confirms that: * HSTU outputs are not passed through the standard vocabulary sampler. * No artificial generated token IDs are produced. * Requests complete after candidate scores are returned. * Candidate scores are returned through prompt_logprobs_dict. * Both Model Runner V1 and Model Runner V2 execution paths are supported. * The HSTU attention backend is initialized and executed successfully. * CUDA Graph execution works in the validated CUDA environment. ### Model Registration and Hugging Face Loading The model registration and Hugging Face loading tests passed. HSTUForCausalLM can be resolved and imported through the vLLM model registry, and the HSTU configuration can be loaded from the Hugging Face model configuration. ### Scheduler and Score-Only Execution The scheduler validation passed for score-only recommendation requests. A recommendation request is correctly completed after candidate scores are produced, even when no new_token_ids are returned. The standard token sampling path is skipped for HSTU requests, and no regular language-model token state update is performed. ### Attention Backend Selection When no explicit attention backend is configured, the HSTU model automatically selects HSTU_ATTN. When an explicit attention backend is configured, the user-provided backend remains authoritative and is not overridden by the HSTU automatic selection logic. ### Current Scope and Limitations This initial integration focuses on bringing HSTU into the vLLM model and serving ecosystem. The current implementation assumes: * Prompt lengths are consistent across users. * Candidate lengths are consistent across users. * HSTU and non-HSTU requests are not mixed in the same batch. * Candidate scores are produced during an unchunked prefill. * Pipeline parallelism is not used. * PD-separated HSTU execution is not supported yet. * KV-cache-based or paged HSTU attention is not supported yet. * request_stage = 1 is not supported. * Each recommendation prompt contains at least one context/candidate pair. These limitations can be addressed in follow-up work after the basic HSTU execution path and serving interface are established.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Preserve SWA replay windows after EAGLE tail pop
signals.text: Fixes #51761 ## Purpose Preserve the sliding-window KV chunks needed when an EAGLE/MTP volatile-tail pop moves the shared replay boundary inside a full-attention alignment segment. The scheduler now derives the replay boundaries from the fixed prompt extent before the first store. It retains only the missing SWA windows as their chunks first become storable, including intermediate boundaries and the EAGLE peek chunk. Decode stores remain monotonic and do not scan below the existing store cursor. ## Test Plan - Exercise 30,208-, 30,272-, and 30,336-token prompt geometries through scheduler store jobs, real CPU offload completion, and an independent replay. - Split prompt storage into two batches with the first batch crossing the replay boundary, then verify a 64-token decode stores only its new SWA tail. - Cover both sliding-window and full-attention EAGLE groups. - Run focused formatting and lint checks on the changed files. ## Test Result - 30,208-token replay restores 30,144 tokens, with the two required C4 keys resident. - The aligned 30,272-token control restores 30,208 tokens with no supplemental keys. - The 30,336-token controls account for full-attention tightening and both EAGLE attention forms. - Focused regression: 4 passed. - Ruff format, Ruff lint, and diff whitespace checks passed. - The broader `TestEagle` class could not be validated in this local CPU snapshot because its request-runner cases are rejected during platform configuration, before their test logic executes. --- - [x] Purpose and linked issue considered. - [x] Test plan provided. - [x] Test results provided. - [x] Documentation impact considered; no user-facing interface changed.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] DSpark: inherit the target's attention backend when the speculative config names none
signals.text: ## Purpose `load_dspark_model` passes `backend=speculative_config.attention_backend` when building the draft's config. That field is `None` unless the user names a backend inside `--speculative-config`, and `None` re-runs backend auto-selection rather than meaning "same as target" — so an explicitly pinned target backend is silently discarded and the draft can pick a different attention class. On DeepSeek V4 with `--attention-config.backend FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, the target builds `DeepseekV4FlashInferMLAAttention` (plain 512B KV row) while the draft falls back to `DeepseekV4FlashMLAAttention`, whose `__init__` rewrites the shared `cache_config.cache_dtype` to `fp8_ds_mla`. The SWA cache is then allocated at 584B/token but still reshaped at `head_dim`, on every rank at first forward: ``` RuntimeError: shape '[-1, 64, 512]' is invalid for input of size 4176917504 vllm/models/deepseek_v4/attention.py, in _fused_qnorm_rope_kv_insert ``` `4176917504 = 111754 * 64 * 584`, the `fp8_ds_mla` geometry. Fall back to the target's backend when the speculative config names none; an explicit `attention_backend` still wins. ## Why this is not a duplicate - **#40611** (open) lets the draft *deliberately differ* from the target. This fixes the *fallback* when nothing is specified; the explicit override still wins. - **#51538** / **#51042** fix a different DSV4 + DSpark defect (`decode_swa_indices` width). Independent of this one and deliberately not included. Each masks the other, verified on one config (DSV4-Pro-0813, TP8 × 2 GB300, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, DSpark k=7): | fixes | result | | --- | --- | | neither | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid (this bug) | | this PR | passes, then fails in #51538's path: `shape '[7, 128]'` invalid | | #51538 | `shape '[-1, 64, 512]'` invalid again (this bug) | | both | engine initializes and serves | ## Test plan `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dspark_topk.py` → **2 passed**. `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dspark/utils.py` → all pass (incl. mypy, ruff). ## Model evaluation aime25, 4 epochs (n=120), temperature 1.0 / top_p 0.95, thinking on, `max_tokens=150000`, DSV4-Pro-0813 on TP8 × 2 GB300, same tree throughout. DSpark rows need #51538 applied too, since both are required to start: | configuration | exact_match | pass@4 | errors | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec | 1.0000 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark | 0.9917 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4` + DSpark (n=360) | 0.9778 | 1.0 | 0 | | `FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV4`, no spec (n=360) | 0.9944 | 1.0 | 0 | Mean acceptance length 3.16 at full concurrency. The DSpark row's single miss is a `length` truncation on the one AIME problem that runs long in every configuration tested, with no repetition loop. No unfixed baseline: the configuration cannot start without this fix. ## AI assistance This work was produced with AI assistance. The submitter has reviewed every changed line, and the tests and evaluations above were executed on the hardware described.

signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Isolate tiering shutdown failures
signals.text: # [Bugfix][KV Offload] Continue tier cleanup after shutdown failures ## Purpose `TieringOffloadingManager.shutdown()` tears down secondary tiers before the CPU primary tier. Previously, an ordinary exception from one secondary tier immediately aborted the loop, skipping all later secondary tiers and the primary tier. The primary tier owns the memoryview and `SharedOffloadRegion` cleanup for the scheduler-side mmap. This change makes normal shutdown follow the same best-effort resource-ownership policy already used for tiering initialization cleanup: every secondary tier is attempted in configuration order, then the primary tier is attempted regardless of earlier ordinary exceptions. Failures remain observable through `logger.exception`, including the secondary tier index, configured tier type, and implementation class. The change intentionally does not catch `BaseException`, retry shutdown calls, or change scheduler and backend behavior. This reduces the graceful-shutdown risk that a secondary teardown exception prevents the primary mmap owner from releasing its resources. It does not address `SIGKILL`, process crashes, or a shutdown call that blocks forever. The most relevant in-tree failure surface is P2P teardown, which releases NIXL and ZMQ resources and can surface ordinary backend exceptions. The same is true for externally configured secondary tiers. File-system and object tiers handle most cleanup errors internally; a blocked lookup or I/O thread is a hang rather than an exception and is outside this change's scope. ## Why this is not a duplicate The duplicate-work search found no open PR that implements per-secondary-tier failure isolation in `TieringOffloadingManager.shutdown()`. This is distinct from #51622, which centralizes cleanup ordering for the CPU worker's GPU-to-CPU and CPU-to-GPU handlers. This change covers the scheduler-side tiering manager and ensures secondary-tier failure cannot skip the primary tier's mmap cleanup. ## Test Plan ```bash .venv/bin/python -m compileall -q \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py uvx --from pre-commit pre-commit run --files \ vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/manager.py \ PR_DESCRIPTION.md git diff --check ``` ## Test Result - `compileall`: passed. - `pre-commit`: all applicable hooks passed. - `git diff --check`: passed. - Model evaluation: not applicable; this only changes shutdown cleanup control flow. ## AI Assistance AI assistance was used for repository inspection, implementation, and this PR description. The human submitter must review every changed line and run the validation they consider appropriate before submitting.

signals.title: [Bugfix] Add opt-out for synchronized FlashInfer autotune (multi-node deadlock without GPUDirect RDMA)
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #52291. Since the FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3 bump (#50892) wired `set_autotune_process_group` into `kernel_warmup.flashinfer_autotune` (design from #48714), multi-node startup deadlocks deterministically during autotuning on clusters whose inter-node transport is host-staged NCCL without GPUDirect RDMA (reproduced on 6× GB10 / DGX Spark class, TP=2 × PP=3): ranks desynchronize between tuning rounds, after which the cross-rank per-tactic timing collective blocks forever — one TP rank enters the next tuning round, its peer never does, both sit in futex wait at 0% GPU and startup never completes (full matrix in the issue: reproduced across FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3 / 0.6.17 / 0.6.18, pip and system NCCL, warm and cold JIT caches; the last pre-#50892 build tunes the identical workload cleanly every time). This PR adds `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DISTRIBUTED_SYNC` (default `1`, current behavior unchanged). Setting it to `0` restores the previous per-rank flow for distributed runs: every rank tunes independently, no autotune process group is set (so no cross-rank collectives run during tuning), and the persistent-cache broadcast is skipped because ranks may select different tactics. ## Test Plan - Deployed on the affected cluster (6× GB10, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3-MXFP8`, TP=2 × PP=3, vLLM `0.27.2rc1.dev54+gb96bcd0b4`, FlashInfer 0.6.18) with the opt-out active. - Compared against the same deployment with default settings, and with `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=mxfp8_gemm`. ## Test Result - Default (synchronized): startup deadlocks in autotune every time (6/6 attempts across image/library permutations). - `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DISTRIBUTED_SYNC=0`: autotune completes on all ranks, startup succeeds, serving verified end-to-end; single-stream throughput 14.4–14.5 tok/s (vs 9.0 tok/s with the op skipped un-tuned) — matching the pre-#50892 baseline. - Single-node and default-path behavior unchanged (the new branch is only taken when `world_size > 1` and the env is explicitly disabled).

signals.title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable fused KDA decode on gfx942 (MI325X)
signals.text: ## Purpose PR #50654 added the fused Kimi-K3 KDA decode kernel (`csrc/libtorch_stable/kimi_k3/fused_kda_decode_kernel_rocm.cu`), but gated it to gfx950 (MI355X) in two places, so it never activates on gfx942 (MI325X): - **Build gate** — `CMakeLists.txt` filtered the HIP source to `gfx950` only, so the kernel was not compiled and `VLLM_ENABLE_FUSED_KDA_DECODE` (and therefore `torch.ops._C.fused_kda_decode`) was never defined on a gfx942-only build. - **Runtime gate** — `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py` ended with `return on_gfx950()`. This change extends both gates to gfx942 as well, so MI325X can take the fused decode path instead of falling back to the three-launch Triton path. The kernel body is unchanged. It uses only CDNA-common primitives — wave64, DPP row/quad permutes (`quad_perm`, `row_half_mirror`, `row_mirror`), `__builtin_nontemporal_load/store`, and bf16 intrinsics — with no MFMA / FP8 / gfx950-only paths, so no source-level changes are required for gfx942. LDS use is ~2.8 KiB/block and register pressure ~130 VGPR, both well within CDNA3 limits. ## Changes - `CMakeLists.txt`: HIP arch filter `gfx950` -> `gfx942|gfx950` (and comment). - `vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/ops/kda_decode.py`: gate `on_gfx950()` -> `on_gfx950() or on_gfx942()`. - `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py`: extend the module skip guard from gfx950 to gfx942 / gfx950 so the correctness suite runs on MI325X. All other backends and the CUDA path are unchanged; the shape/dtype/head-count guards in `is_fused_kda_decode_supported()` are unchanged. ## Performance The kernel-level win is large, but the end-to-end win on MI325X is currently small: the Kimi-K3 decode step is dominated by the MXFP4 MoE (int4) and the MLA attention plus the TP8 collectives, which dwarf the KDA linear-attention block. The fusion removes ~66 us of per-layer kernel time (mostly launch overhead), but that is a small fraction of today's total per-token cost. It should become more visible once #50817 (MXFP4 MoE Triton a16w4 for gfx942) lands and shrinks the dominant MoE cost — the fixed KDA saving then represents a larger share of a smaller decode step. ### End-to-end (tp8, 256-in / 256-out, max-concurrency 4) | Metric | Triton fallback | Fused KDA | Delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 425.95 | 422.66 | -0.77% | | P99 TPOT (ms) | 427.64 | 424.19 | -0.81% | | Output tok/s | 9.29 | 9.36 | +0.75% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 1577.24 | 1574.03 | -0.20% (flat) | TTFT is unchanged, as expected for a decode-only kernel. ### Per-layer kernel sequence (torch profiler medians, us) Baseline runs the KDA decode as ~16 separate kernels per layer — the conv1d update, the recurrent delta-rule step, and the gated output RMSNorm decomposed into a chain of launch-overhead-bound (~4 us floor) elementwise ops. Fused collapses all of them into a single kernel: | # | Baseline kernel | us | Fused kernel | us | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | _causal_conv1d_update_kernel | 5.01 | kda_decode_fusion_kernel<true, 12, true, true, true> | 7.77 | | 2 | fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel | 6.45 | | | | 3 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.37 | | | | 4 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.41 | | | | 5 | pow (tensor, scalar) | 4.41 | | | | 6 | reduce Mean | 5.01 | | | | 7 | add | 4.45 | | | | 8 | rsqrt | 4.37 | | | | 9 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 10 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.17 | | | | 11 | mul | 4.21 | | | | 12 | bfloat16->float32 copy | 4.45 | | | | 13 | sigmoid | 5.05 | | | | 14 | mul | 4.33 | | | | 15 | float32->bfloat16 copy | 4.49 | | | | 16 | __amd_rocclr_copyBuffer | 4.57 | | | | | **total (16 kernels)** | **~73.96** | **total (1 kernel)** | **7.77** | ~9.5x less kernel time for the KDA decode block (~74 -> 7.8 us/layer). The `12` template arg is 12 heads/rank (96 KDA heads at TP8). Across the model's KDA layers (~69 per the kernel header) that is ~4.6 ms/token of raw kernel time removed, in the same ballpark as the ~3.3 ms/token TPOT drop measured above (the remainder overlaps with other work). ## Not a duplicate - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "KDA decode gfx942"` - `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "fused_kda_decode MI325"` ## Test Plan Run on an MI325X (gfx942) box after building with gfx942 in the arch list: 1. Build compiles the kernel and registers the op: `python -c "import torch, vllm; print(hasattr(torch.ops._C, 'fused_kda_decode'))"` -> expect `True`. 2. Kernel correctness: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_amd_kda_decode.py -v` 3. Model accuracy (output-affecting change) — serve Kimi-K3 on MI325X and run gsm8k, compared against the Triton fallback path: `make gsm8k` 4. Decode latency / throughput before vs after (fused vs Triton fallback): `make bench-kda-mi325` ## Test Result - Op registered: **True** on the gfx942 build (`hasattr(torch.ops._C, "fused_kda_decode")`); the fused kernel appears in the trace (see Performance). - Latency/throughput: **-0.77% mean TPOT**, +0.75% output tok/s - gsm8k (fused vs Triton): **parity** — both 1.00 exact_match on flexible-extract and strict-match (5-shot, limit=100, stderr 0). The fused kernel matches the Triton fallback exactly. - `test_amd_kda_decode.py`: **12/12 passed** on MI325X (gfx942) — fused output matches the Triton reference across heads {12, 24, 96} x tokens {1, 7, 128}, plus the null-slot, no-output-norm, and padding edge cases. ## Checklist - [x] Compiles for gfx942 (kernel present in the .so with gfx942 codegen) - [x] `test_amd_kda_decode.py` passes on MI325X (12/12) - [x] gsm8k parity with the Triton path - [x] AI assistance used (see below) ## AI assistance This change was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). A human must review every line and run the build, tests, and eval on MI325X hardware before merge; the correctness and accuracy results above are not yet filled in.

signals.title: [bot] Enable google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant inference on Intel XPU
signals.text: ## Motivation `google/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant` uses the `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM` architecture and `gemma4_assistant` config type, which are not yet recognized by vLLM or the installed Transformers version. This PR adds the minimal plumbing to load and run this model. ## Technical Details 1. **Model registry**: Map `Gemma4AssistantForCausalLM` → `Gemma4ForCausalLM` (same architecture, different config wrapper). 2. **Config classes**: Add `Gemma4AssistantConfig` and `Gemma4TextConfig` in `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/gemma4.py` so the checkpoint can be loaded without a Transformers upgrade. 3. **Config registry**: Register `gemma4_assistant` and `gemma4_text` model types. 4. **Model arch config convertor**: Register `gemma4_assistant` → `Gemma4ModelArchConfigConvertor`. 5. **KV shared layer fix**: Guard `first_kv_shared_layer_idx` with `> 0` to prevent false-positive shared-layer activation when the index is 0 (E2B has `num_kv_shared_layers=0`). 6. **Tokenizer fix**: Handle `extra_special_tokens` being a list instead of a dict (shipped by the gemma4_assistant tokenizer config), which causes an `AttributeError` in older Transformers. ## Testing - Model loads and generates correct output on Intel XPU (Arc Pro B60, Max 1550). - AI assistance was used (opencode agent). ## FYI This PR was generated with AI assistance.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Sync speculative draft tokens across PP ranks
signals.text: ## Purpose In Model Runner V2, speculative proposal runs only on the last pipeline rank. The resulting next-step draft tokens are written to that rank's request state, but the non-last ranks keep stale or zero-initialized draft tokens. Those ranks then reconstruct a different speculative verification input in the following PP step. This PR carries the next-step draft tokens together with the existing sampled-token PP broadcast and restores sampled and draft state together when the same delayed PP queue slot is consumed. It adds no collective and leaves non-PP paths unchanged. The transport is enabled for every speculative method that passes the existing MRV2 PP validation; unsupported methods still fail before `PPHandler` construction. This intentionally isolates only the draft-token synchronization issue from #46994. It does not include model enablement, model-specific projections, sparse-MLA backend changes, quantization, or weight-loading changes, so this correctness fix can be reviewed and merged independently. ## Test Plan ```bash pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ruff check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ruff format --check vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py \ vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py ``` The corresponding MTP+PP path was also exercised with the vLLM Ascend backend using real-weight single-request inference and GSM8K evaluation. ## Test Result - Ruff check passed. - Ruff format check passed for all three changed files. - Targeted unit tests passed in the Ascend test container: `2 passed`. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing the test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [x] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. signals.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Coordinate mmap host registration
signals.text: ## Purpose Fixes #51762. Coordinate host registration across all TP x PCP x PP workers that map the same CPU KV-offload region. Workers now wait for a mapping fence, register in deterministic model-rank order, and make one group-wide decision from the registration results. If a normal registration call fails, every successful worker unregisters and the whole group keeps the existing unpinned fallback. Setup or registration exceptions and incomplete rollbacks fail startup only after all workers have finished the transaction. The unpinned fallback also forces the DMA copy path so a GPU kernel never dereferences pageable host memory. ## Related Work This does not duplicate the existing host-registration PRs: - #50070 keeps registration and pending-error cleanup on the same CUDA runtime handle, but does not coordinate workers or make their pinning state coherent. - #51081 splits very large registrations into chunks to avoid the 512 GiB registration ceiling, but does not coordinate concurrent worker outcomes. - #51956 adds XPU host registration and platform dispatch, but does not address mixed pinned and unpinned CUDA/ROCm workers sharing one mmap region. This PR is scoped to serializing registration across the TP x PCP x PP workers that share an engine mmap, making one group-wide decision, rolling back partial success, and selecting a safe DMA path after an unpinned fallback. ## Test Plan - Exercise two local Gloo processes for all-success, return-code failure, registration setup exception, and registration exception outcomes. - Verify ordinary fallback unregisters successful workers exactly once and rollback failures retain registration ownership for cleanup. - Verify model-rank ordering spans TP x PCP x PP without crossing DP engines. - Verify unpinned CPU-to-GPU transfers select the DMA implementation. ## Test Result - Diff whitespace validation passed. - Python AST parsing passed for both changed files. - An isolated semantic smoke test passed for model-rank ordering, collective ordering, coherent rollback, setup failure, and rollback failure. - The focused pytest suite could not start because the prepared checkout did not contain pytest, and dependency installation was unavailable. The added tests should be run in CI with: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \ -k "pin_mmap_region or model_parallel_coordination or unpinned_cpu_to_gpu or worker_uses_model_parallel_coordination" \ -q ```

signals.title: [Frontend] shutdown engine core and its sub processes asap when initializing
signals.text: <!-- markdownlint-disable --> PLEASE FILL IN THE PR DESCRIPTION HERE ENSURING ALL CHECKLIST ITEMS (AT THE BOTTOM) HAVE BEEN CONSIDERED. ## Purpose This is a follow up after #43417. After #43417 merged, if a frontend process exits unexpected, for example, in a multi api process setup env, `run_multi_api_server` will call `finally` and engine core proc manager shutdown function will be called. For now, engine core proc has been busying in initializing model executor processes and engine core process has not register a custom signal handler. Thus, a SIGTERM signal will be sent to engine core process and engine core process will exit and leaving its subprocess, model executor processes, as they are. Finally these model executor processes will only exit when they run to an exception or completion wasting GPU resources. We need to shutdown engine core process and all its subprocesses asap. ## Test Plan 1. setting `export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=120` 2. run `vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B --max-num-seqs 512 --renderer-num-workers 1 --tensor-parallel-size 2 --pipeline_parallel_size 2 --data-parallel-size 1` ## Test Result a log will be record soon after the timeout exception is raised. ``` RuntimeError: Frontend process failed during engine core initialization. signals.title: [Perf][Nemotron] Skip redundant latent-MoE all-reduce at TP>1 (~13% decode win)
signals.text: ## Purpose **Nemotron-3 super decode regressed ~13% between v0.26.0 and v0.27.x at TP>1. This PR restores it.** tp4, concurrency 1 | Nemotron-3 Super 120B-A12B BF16 | v0.26.0 | v0.27.1 | v0.27.1 + this PR | |---|---|---|---| | inter-token latency | 4.08 ms | 4.60 ms (+12.8%) | **4.07 ms** | | output tok/s per user | 245.0 | 217.2 (−11.4%) | **246.0** | **inter-token latency** | models | v0.26.0 | v0.27.1 | v0.27.1 + this PR | |---|---|---|---| | Super 120B-A12B BF16 | 4.07 ms | 4.64 ms (**+13.8%**) | **4.08 ms** | | Ultra 550B-A55B NVFP4 | 6.86 ms† | 7.21 ms | **6.79 ms** | No existing issue found ### Root cause [`_maybe_reduce_routed_output_before_transform()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L434-L453), added in v0.27.0rc1, all-reduces the routed output in latent space *before* `routed_output_transform` is applied, since that transform may be non-linear. [The combined output is then all-reduced again](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L455-L495) on the late path. So **every latent-MoE layer at TP>1 or EP>1 issues two tensor-parallel all-reduces per token instead of one** ([call site](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L742-L749)). The function does not exist in v0.26.0. `NemotronH` is hit because it passes [`fc2_latent_proj` as its `routed_output_transform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L226). ### The fix The early reduce is only needed when the transform does not commute with the sum over ranks. A bias-free linear transform does commute — `sum_r W x_r == W sum_r x_r` — so reducing once *after* it is equivalent and costs one collective instead of two. With a bias it does not, since `sum_r (W x_r + b) == W sum_r x_r + R*b`. This adds an opt-in `reduce_commutative` attribute on the transform, **defaulting to `False` so every model that does not set it is byte-for-byte unchanged.** `NemotronH` sets it from `not config.mlp_bias`; its [`fc2_latent_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L194-L201) is a `ReplicatedLinear`, identical on every rank. **Kimi K3 is unchanged.** Its [`KimiRoutedOutputTransform`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/model.py#L295-L302) wraps an `RMSNorm`, which is non-linear and genuinely needs the early reduce. It never sets the attribute, so both collectives are retained. <details> <summary>Interactions checked, quantised transforms, and the alternative considered</summary> **Interactions with the surrounding reduce logic** - [`skip_final_all_reduce`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L468-L473) asserts against [`self._fused_output_is_reduced`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/moe_runner.py#L403-L408), a property of the combine kernel that this PR does not touch, so the assertion is unaffected. - For `NemotronH`, `reduce_results` defaults to `True` — the [`reduce_results=False`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_h.py#L180) nearby is on the *shared_experts* MLP, not the FusedMoE — so `skip_final_all_reduce == False` and the late all-reduce always fires. **Quantised transforms** When the transform is quantised, input quantisation is a non-linear step, so `sum_r T(x_r)` and `T(sum_r x_r)` differ by more than float summation order. This is not introduced by this PR — it is what v0.26.0 did for those checkpoints — but stating it plainly: commutativity holds exactly for the unquantised bias-free linear case, and to within quantisation error otherwise. Measurements below are bf16. **Alternative: wire NemotronH to `LatentMoERunner`** [`LatentMoERunner`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L52) already implements a fused single-collective path, and pointing `NemotronH` at it would also remove the extra collective. I did not pursue it because: 1. It now lives under `vllm/models/kimi_k3/`, moved there by [#50678](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50678) ([`b9d1e2437e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/b9d1e2437e1ad6d98d301939949072b5c56dfef1)) after v0.27.1 — upstream has deliberately scoped it to K3. 2. It assumes K3's transform shape, reading [`transform.norm` and `transform.up_proj`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d4c24e6f5d1864bc81ad0769097e00b9042178ca/vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/latent_moe_runner.py#L216-L224), whereas `NemotronH` passes a bare `ReplicatedLinear`. It would need an adapter — a larger blast radius than this guard. Happy to be redirected. The attribute name/API is a bikeshed I have no attachment to; a `Protocol` or a flag on `FusedMoEConfig` would work as well. </details> ## Test Plan 4x GB300 (sm_103), stock upstream containers `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.26.0` and `:v0.27.1`, no NCCL env overrides. Public checkpoint [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16) (`moe_latent_size=1024`, `mlp_bias=false`). Every flag below exists in both releases, so the arms differ only by vLLM version. ```bash # 1. Serve (--tensor-parallel-size 1 for the negative control) vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \ --served-model-name nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b \ --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --max-model-len 2200 --max-num-seqs 128 \ --attention-backend FLASHINFER --trust-remote-code \ --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-cache-mode align \ --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --port 8000 # 2. Benchmark (aiperf 0.12.0), C over 1, 8, 32, 64 aiperf profile --url localhost:8000 --model nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b \ --tokenizer nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \ --endpoint-type completions --tokenizer-trust-remote-code --streaming \ --extra-inputs "min_tokens:1000" --extra-inputs "max_tokens:1000" \ --extra-inputs "ignore_eos:true" \ --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 1000 --synthetic-input-tokens-stddev 0 \ --output-tokens-mean 1000 --output-tokens-stddev 0 \ --concurrency ${C} --request-count $((5 * C)) --warmup-request-count 1 # 3. Accuracy (server as above but --max-model-len 4096) lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=nemotron-super-v3-120b-a12b,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False,tokenizer=nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \ --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 32 ``` Controls: **tp1** (the early reduce is gated on `tp_size > 1 or ep_size > 1`, so tp1 must show no change); **same-node** v0.26.0 vs v0.27.1, with v0.27.1 also run on a second node to quantify node variation; patch state asserted per run by reading the installed `moe_runner.py` / `nemotron_h.py` out of `site-packages`. ## Test Result ### tp4 concurrency sweep Two runs per arm at concurrency 1; run-to-run range was 0.00 ms. | inter-token latency (ms) | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 | |---|---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | 4.08 | 6.23 | 9.88 | 12.18 | | v0.27.1 | 4.60 | 6.63 | 10.39 | 13.09 | | v0.27.1 + this PR | **4.07** | **6.11** | **9.88** | **12.21** | | v0.27.1 regression | +12.83% | +6.51% | +5.18% | +7.47% | | output tok/s per user | c=1 | c=8 | c=32 | c=64 | |---|---|---|---|---| | v0.26.0 | 245.02 | 160.72 | 101.25 | 82.13 | | v0.27.1 | 217.17 | 150.85 | 96.26 | 76.42 | | v0.27.1 + this PR | **246.00** | **163.70** | **101.18** | **81.90** | v0.26.0 performance is restored at every concurrency. The win is largest at low concurrency and shrinks as batch grows — expected, since at small batch these collectives are latency-bound so their *count* dominates, while at larger batch they become bandwidth-bound and the surviving reduce (4096-wide hidden dim) is larger than the removed one (1024-wide latent dim). It is not a trade-off at any measured point. | [`nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4) | ITL (ms) | tok/s per user | |---|---|---| | v0.27.1 | 7.21 | 138.71 | | v0.27.1 + this PR | **6.79** | **147.22** | | Δ | **−5.8%** | **+6.1%** | ### Controls - **tp1 negative control:** ITL 6.22 ms (v0.26.0) vs 6.20 ms (v0.27.1), −0.30%. No difference, as the TP gate predicts. - **Node-to-node variation:** v0.27.1 on two different GB300 nodes, 4.63 vs 4.60 ms — 0.65%, far below the 12.83% effect. ### Accuracy — gsm8k, 5-shot, greedy, tp4, full 1319 questions Both arms on the same node in the same container, differing only by this patch: | checkpoint | arm | flexible-extract | strict-match | |---|---|---|---| | Super BF16 | v0.27.1 | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9181 ± 0.0076 | | Super BF16 | + this PR | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9166 ± 0.0076 | | Ultra NVFP4 | v0.27.1 | 0.9363 ± 0.0067 | 0.9340 ± 0.0068 | | Ultra NVFP4 | + this PR | 0.9431 ± 0.0064 | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 | +0.0008 and −0.0015, i.e. 0.1 and 0.2 standard errors — no measurable difference. Bitwise identity is not expected: moving the all-reduce past a linear map changes floating-point summation order. --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [x] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [x] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [x] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. Documentation: no update needed — no public API change, no new model, and the `reduce_commutative` contract is documented in the docstring of `_maybe_reduce_routed_output_before_transform`. </details>

signals.title: [bot] Fix Gemma4 BOS token handling for raw-text prompts on XPU
signals.text: ## Motivation The Gemma4 multimodal processor overrode `add_special_tokens=False` in `get_default_tok_params()`, which stripped the BOS token from all prompts. This caused garbled/repetitive output (e.g. *"the capital of France is the capital of France is..."*) because the model expects a leading BOS token. This particularly affected raw-text prompts such as those used by `lm_eval` (GSM8k benchmarks), where no chat template injects a literal `<bos>`. ## Technical Details - **Root cause**: `Gemma4ProcessingInfo.get_default_tok_params()` set `add_special_tokens=False`, preventing the tokenizer from prepending BOS. - **Fix**: Remove the override so the base-class default (`add_special_tokens=True`) is used. The Gemma4 tokenizer already has `add_bos_token=False`, so BOS is only added via `add_special_tokens`. Chat-template prompts that embed a literal `<bos>` won't get double-BOS. - **File changed**: `vllm/model_executor/models/gemma4_mm.py` (1 file, 22 lines) ## Performance / Accuracy - **Model**: `google/gemma-4-E2B` on Intel Arc Pro B60 (XPU) - **GSM8k 5-shot strict (250 samples)**: 20.8% — expected for a 2B parameter model - **Decode speed**: ~25 tok/s (~40 ms/tok) - **No double-BOS regression**: Verified chat-template prompts still produce correct single-BOS sequences

signals.title: [Bugfix][Ray] Strip brackets from IPv6 node IP for MessageQueue connect_ip
signals.text: ## Purpose On IPv6-only clusters, `ray.util.get_node_ip_address()` can return an IPv6 address wrapped in brackets (e.g. `[fe80::1]`; a documented Ray behavior). `RayExecutorV2` passed this value straight into `MessageQueue(connect_ip=...)` at two call sites: - `RayWorkerProc._init_message_queues` (`worker_response_mq`) - `RayExecutorV2._init_executor` (`rpc_broadcast_mq`) Inside `MessageQueue`, the branch that enables IPv6 is guarded by `is_valid_ipv6_address(connect_ip)`, which is backed by `ipaddress.IPv6Address(...)`. That parser **rejects the bracketed form**: ``` ::1 -> valid [::1] -> INVALID <- what Ray returns fe80::1 -> valid [fe80::1] -> INVALID <- what Ray returns ``` Consequently `remote_addr_ipv6` stayed `False`, the ZMQ socket never had `IPV6` enabled, and the subsequent `bind`/`connect` to the bracketed address failed. The exported `Handle` also carried `remote_addr_ipv6=False`, so remote readers connected without IPv6 support and failed too. ## Fix Normalize the Ray node IP by stripping brackets before handing it to `MessageQueue`. `MessageQueue` then re-brackets the bare address itself (its existing `connect_ip = f"[{connect_ip}]"` path). This keeps the "connect_ip is a bare address" contract that `shm_broadcast` already assumes. IPv4 and already-bare IPv6 addresses are unaffected — `.strip("[]")` only removes leading/trailing brackets, which never appear in an IPv4 address. ## Why this is not a duplicate - No open PR or issue addresses bracketed-IPv6 `connect_ip` in `RayExecutorV2` (searched `get_node_ip_address`, `connect_ip ipv6`, `ray_executor_v2 ipv6`). - #50969 also touches `ray_executor_v2.py`, but it fixes the **TCPStore port bind TOCTOU race** (`_select_tcpstore_port` / `distributed_init_method`). It does not touch the `MessageQueue` `connect_ip` values and is an orthogonal change. - #18986 (closed) concerned data-parallel IPv6 host recognition, a different code path. ## Test Plan / Results Behavior of the normalization + downstream validity check, verified locally: ``` '[fe80::1]' -> 'fe80::1' is_valid_ipv6=True 'fe80::1' -> 'fe80::1' is_valid_ipv6=True '[::1]' -> '::1' is_valid_ipv6=True '::1' -> '::1' is_valid_ipv6=True '10.0.0.1' -> '10.0.0.1' is_valid_ipv6=False (unchanged) '127.0.0.1' -> '127.0.0.1' is_valid_ipv6=False (unchanged) ``` Lint (pre-commit) on the changed file: ```bash pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py # Passed pre-commit run ruff-format --files vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py # Passed ``` Model evaluation is not applicable: this change only affects startup address normalization for the control-plane MessageQueue and does not alter model execution or outputs. ## AI disclosure AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and drafting. The human submitter has reviewed every changed line and can defend the change and tests end-to-end.

Updates `tokenizers` from 0.22.2 to 0.23.1
Release notes

Sourced from tokenizers's releases.

Release v0.23.1

TL;DR

tokenizers 0.23.1 is the first proper stable release in the 0.23 line — 0.23.0 only ever shipped as rc0 because the release pipeline itself was broken (Node side hadn't shipped multi-platform binaries since 2023, Python side was on pyo3 0.27 without free-threaded support). 0.23.1 is the version where everything actually goes out the door together: full Node multi-platform wheels for the first time in years, Python 3.14 (regular and free-threaded 3.14t), full type hints for every Python class, and a stack of measurable perf wins on the BPE / added-vocab hot paths.

There is no functional 0.23.0 published — we tag 0.23.1 directly so users don't accidentally pull a never-shipped version.

🚨 Breaking changes

  • Drop Python 3.9 (#1952) — requires-python = ">=3.10"; 3.9 users stay on 0.22.x.
  • add_tokens normalizes content at insertion (#1995) — re-saved tokenizer.json may differ in the added_tokens block. Existing files load unchanged.
  • Type stubs are precise (#1928, #1997) — methods that returned Any now return real types; mypy --strict may surface previously-hidden errors. Stub layout also moved from tokenizers/<sub>/__init__.pyi to tokenizers/<sub>.pyi. This breaks the surface of some of the processors like RobertaProcessign's __init__ .
  • 3.14t-only: setters/getters return PyResult<T> because of Arc<RwLock<Tokenizer>>; a poisoned lock surfaces as PyException instead of a panic.

⚡ Performance — measured locally on this Mac, not lifted from PRs

Run with cargo bench --bench <name> -- --save-baseline v0_22_2 on v0.22.2, then --baseline v0_22_2 on v0.23.1. Numbers are point-in-time wall clock on a single laptop; relative deltas are what matters, absolute numbers will differ on CI hardware.

Added-vocabulary deserialize — the headline win (#1995, #1999)

bench: improve added_vocab_deserialize to reflect real-world workloads (#2000) is now representative of how transformers actually loads tokenizer.json files. The combined effect of daachorse for the matching automaton plus the normalize-on-insert refactor is enormous on this workload:

benchmark v0.22.2 v0.23.1 change
100k tokens, special, no norm ~410 ms 248 ms −40%
100k tokens, non-special, no norm ~7.1 s 273 ms −96%
100k tokens, special, NFKC ~395 ms 235 ms −40%
100k tokens, non-special, NFKC ~7.4 s 290 ms −96%
400k tokens, special, no norm ~15 s 980 ms −94%

Real-world impact: loading a Llama-3-style tokenizer with a large set of added tokens dropped from "noticeable pause" to "instant".

BPE encode

benchmark v0.22.2 v0.23.1 change
BPE GPT2 encode batch, no cache 530 ms 446 ms −16%
BPE GPT2 encode batch (cached) 690 ms 685 ms noise
BPE GPT2 encode (single) 1.95 s 1.94 s noise
BPE Train (small) 32.6 ms 31.5 ms −3%
BPE Train (big) 1.01 s 988 ms −2%

The BPE per-thread cache PR (#2028) shows much larger wins on highly-parallel workloads (+47–62% at 88+ threads on a server box, per the PR's own measurements on Vera). Single-thread batch numbers above are flat or slightly improved because cache-hit overhead was already low without contention.

signals.title: [Bugfix][Model Runner V2][Spec Decode] Fix off-by-one in bad_words draft-prefix matching
signals.text: ## Purpose Fix an off-by-one in the spec-decode branch of `_bad_words_kernel` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/bad_words.py`), present since the kernel was introduced in #33433. The sampler passes `input_ids` gathered at `logits_indices`, so for a spec-decode request the per-request local layout is: local position 0 = last committed sampled token, local position j = draft token d_{j-1}. The sibling kernels index draft tokens accordingly (`_penalties_kernel` uses `start_idx + prev_pos + 1`; thinking budget's `_load_effective_token` uses `+ 1` with an explicit comment). `_bad_words_kernel` read `input_ids_ptr + cur_req_first_pos + spec_offset` without the `+ 1`, so every draft-region read was shifted back by one token (the boundary token was read twice). Consequences when bad_words and speculative decoding are combined and a multi-token bad word's prefix window reaches into the draft tokens: - prefix matches ending in the draft region are missed (the banned token can be sampled/accepted); - matches spanning the committed/draft boundary fire one verification row late; - the duplicated boundary read can spuriously match and ban an innocent token. Single-token bad words and non-spec rows are unaffected. Model Runner V1 has a separate implementation and is unaffected. **Not a duplicate:** searched open PRs/issues for `bad_words` + spec decode / off-by-one / `_bad_words_kernel`; no existing fix found (closest is #34213, which only touches penalties). ## Test Plan New unit test (first coverage for this kernel), following the pattern of `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py`: ```bash pytest -v tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_bad_words.py ``` Scenario: committed output `[10, 11]`, draft tokens `[12, 13]`. The core regression case is the boundary-spanning prefix (`[11, 12, 30]` must mask at the row where the prefix completes, not one row later); the other three cases pin the remaining coverage axes: a positive match at draft offset >= 1 (`[12, 13, 40]`), a no-double-count guard for the boundary token (`[11, 11, 50]`), and a committed-only baseline (`[10, 11, 60]`). Assertions compare the full logits tensor. ## Test Result Ran on an A100 SXM4 80GB (torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, Python 3.11), with the branch installed editable via `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED` (nightly x86_64 wheel `66728feb1`): - **With the fix (HEAD): `4 passed`.** - **With the pre-fix kernel** (parent commit's `bad_words.py` swapped in): **`3 failed, 1 passed`** — exactly the three spec-branch cases fail; the committed-only baseline passes. - `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass on both changed files. - Cross-validation: the kernel's scalar loop was transcribed to pure Python and checked against an independent reference matcher over 20,000 randomized spec-decode scenarios; with the `+ 1` the kernel matches the reference in all cases, without it ~24% of scenarios diverge. AI assistance was used for this change (Claude); I have reviewed every changed line.
signals.author: jyan-R

signals.title: [LoRA] Avoid false target matches for unsupported module types
signals.text: LoRA target matching previously relied only on module-name suffixes. This can produce false matches when modules with the same suffix have different runtime types. This behavior was reported in [this Gemma 4 LoRA test](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42662#issuecomment-4830505389). The vision tower emitted warnings for modules such as: - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj` - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.mlp.down_proj` These modules are `Gemma4ClippableLinear` containers and cannot be wrapped directly. However, LoRA was successfully loaded into their inner linear layers: - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.linear` - `vision_tower.encoder.layers.0.mlp.down_proj.linear` The warnings were therefore false alarms caused by suffix-only matching. This PR passes the runtime module instance to `is_supported_lora_module` and checks both the module-name suffix and its actual type. Supported inner linear layers continue to receive LoRA, while unsupported container modules with the same suffix are skipped. ## Purpose ## Test Plan ## Test Result --- <details> <summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary> - [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)". - [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command. - [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results - [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model. </details>

signals.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Disable TRTLLM NVFP4 monolithic backend for non-gated MoE (corrupt output on SM100)
signals.text: ## Purpose Immediate mitigation for #52308: the `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` monolithic NVFP4 MoE backend produces **semantically corrupt output for non-gated (ReLU²) MoE models on SM100** (e.g. `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-NVFP4` on B200 — fluent but wrong output, 100% deterministic under greedy decoding). This PR quarantines only the non-gated variant: `TrtLlmNvFp4ExpertsMonolithic._supports_no_act_and_mul()` returns False, so backend auto-selection falls through to `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`, which is numerically correct for these models on both SM100 and SM120. The predicate is consulted only when `moe_config.is_act_and_mul` is False (`modular_kernel.py`), so **gated MoE models keep the monolithic backend unchanged**. The kernel-level root cause inside the monolithic bundle (pad/scale-interleave contract, non-gated scale plumbing, in-kernel `n_group=1` routing — see the issue analysis) remains open and tracked in #52308; this change restores correct output for affected models by default while that is investigated. ## Evidence / model evaluation A/B/A on the same B200, same checkpoint, vLLM v0.27.0, TP=1, greedy (`temperature=0`), prompt `The capital of France is`: | Run | MoE backend | Top-1 logprob | Semantic probes (Paris / 2+2 / sequence) | |---|---|---|---| | A (default) | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` monolithic | `' **' -2.0724` (no content token in top-5) | 0/3 | | B | `flashinfer_cutlass` (what this PR makes the default for non-gated) | `' Paris' -0.0278` | 3/3 | | A′ (revert) | `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` monolithic | broken logprobs reproduce **bit-identically** (10 decimals) | 0/3 | The same checkpoint is correct out-of-the-box on SM120 (RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell), which never selects the monolithic path (`_supports_current_device()` requires `is_device_capability_family(100)`). ## Test plan - On-GPU behavioral verification above: this PR's effect is exactly equivalent to `--moe-backend=flashinfer_cutlass`, which was verified to fully heal the model on B200 (and reverting reproduces the failure deterministically). - Selection can be confirmed in server logs: `Using 'flashinfer_cutlass' NvFp4 MoE backend out of potential backends: [...]` replaces the trtllm selection for non-gated models; no log change for gated models. - Change is a capability predicate flip + docstring only; no kernel or numeric code touched. I did not run the full unit suite locally (dev box has no CUDA GPU); happy to add/extend an oracle selection test asserting non-gated ⇒ not `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` if maintainers want it in this PR rather than alongside the root-cause fix. ## Non-duplication - `gh pr list --search "52308 in:body"` → none. - Searched open PRs for `nvfp4 moe nemotron` and `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe`: nearest matches are #36039 (adds trtllm MoE unit tests — complementary) and historical #36725 ("Fix TRTLLM NVFP4 Routing Kernel Precision" — prior art showing this kernel family has had routing-precision issues; a revert draft #37945 exists). No open PR quarantines the non-gated monolithic path or otherwise addresses #52308. ## AI assistance disclosure This change was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed every changed line, performed the on-GPU A/B/A verification, and can defend the change end-to-end. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
